events.description: Manx National Theatre is proud to present the world premiere of a spectacular new musical - The Theatre Architect. Boasting 13 sparkling new original songs - echoing large scale West-End-style musical numbers and opera; sitting alongside both uplifting and heart-breaking solos and duets. The Theatre Architect tells a true story of love and passion, based on Britain's most successful theatre architect - Frank Matcham - Designer of the Isle of Man's very own "Jewel in the Crown" - The beautiful Gaiety Theatre and Opera House. Be the first to enjoy this wonderful new show before it hits the UK!

events.title: Rock of Ages
events.description: Coming to the Gaiety Theatre in October 2026, Centre Stage Productions proudly present the smash-hit musical comedy Rock of Ages. This outrageously funny Broadway sensation is an unapologetically cheesy jukebox musical and a hilarious love letter to the glam rock era of the 1980s. Packed with iconic anthems from bands like Poison, Styx, Whitesnake and more, it’s loud, ridiculous, and enormous fun. Set on L.A.’s legendary Sunset Strip, Rock of Ages is packed with over 25 iconic rock anthems, including We Built This City, The Final Countdown, Here I Go Again, Can’t Fight This Feeling, I Wanna Rock, I Want To Know What Love Is, and many more. The year is 1987, and fabled West Hollywood club the Bourbon Room - a gritty but beloved rock club on the Sunset Strip - is fighting for survival. When bright-eyed young hopeful Sherrie, a small-town girl who wants to make it as an actress, arrives in town, she bumps into Drew, a busboy with dreams of rock and roll stardom. Love-struck Drew convinces the club owner to hire Sherrie, and the stage seems set for their romance. But when German developers threaten to tear down the Strip and arrogant rockstar Stacee Jaxx blows into town, dreams, romances and the future of the Bourbon Room are thrown into chaos. Rock of Ages is packed with outrageous characters, over-the-top comedy, and wall-to-wall rock anthems. It’s loud. It’s outrageous. It’s gloriously ridiculous. And it’s guaranteed to be the ultimate night of pure 80s rock nostalgia. Sponsored by IFGL, and supported by the Isle of Man Arts Council, Isle of Man Steam Packet Company, and 3FM.

events.title: Dinosaur World Live
events.description: Here by roaring demand, the international smash hit Dinosaur World Live returns this summer! And this time they're coming to the Gaiety Theatre! Don’t miss this award-winning interactive adventure for all the family – featuring the biggest and best dinosaur puppets live on stage! Step into a prehistoric world of astonishing (and remarkably life-like) creatures. Meet an incredible line-up of dinosaurs, including every child's favourite flesh-eating giant, the Tyrannosaurus Rex, alongside a Triceratops, Giraffatitan, Microraptor and Segnosaurus! A special meet and greet after the show offers all our brave explorers the chance to make a new dinosaur friend. Packed with fun, dino-mite discoveries, this mind-expanding Jurassic adventure is not to be missed. Book now before tickets become extinct! ★★★★★ ‘Great fun. Highly recommended for all ages’ - What’s Good To Do ★★★★ 'A spectacular interactive show!' - OK! Magazine ★★★★ ‘The perfect family show. Educational and entertaining’ - The Reviews Hub

events.title: Murder on the Orient Express
events.description: Parker & Snell Company proudly presents the Isle of Man premiere of Agatha Christie's classic thriller, Murder on the Orient Express. A luxury train. A snowbound journey. A brutal murder. When the world-famous Orient Express becomes trapped by deep snow, an American millionaire is found murdered in his locked compartment. With every passenger a suspect and no one able to leave the train, the world-famous Belgian detective Hercule Poirot must untangle a web of secrets, lies and hidden motives before the killer strikes again. Packed with suspense, intrigue and unforgettable characters, this gripping thriller builds towards one of the most celebrated finales in crime fiction. Stylish, witty and utterly compelling, Murder on the Orient Express is a timeless whodunnit that remains one of the greatest detective stories ever written. Join us for an unforgettable journey aboard the Orient Express – for four performances only.

events.title: Carry On Up Prospect Hill
events.description: “Wake up Manxies, we’ve got something to say now please. It’s late September that we really have to fill up Keys”. Let us entertain you, with local performers delivering some very famous songs – but with the lyrics amended, to cover the ups and downs of the election of Members of The House of Keys. Laugh, join in, and of course, dig deep into your pockets to support four Local Charities – Hospice Isle of Man, Forget Me Not, Naseem’s Manx Brain Tumour Charity and Manx National Heritage. Songs include: The end of the current Parliament: “We’re all going on a Keys House holiday”, “Imagine there’s no Tynwald” Preparing for an election: “If I were a Tynwald Man”, “I never will be an MHK, no more” Pleading for votes: “Please vote for me Ayre and Michael”, “Gimme, Gimme, Gimme your votes in the morning” Misery from the losers: “Yesterday, all my voters seemed to fade away”, “Tragedy” Joy from the winners: “Thank you for the yes vote”, “When you walk, in Tynwald.”

events.title: The Great British Bake Off - The Musical
events.description: Inspired by the beloved TV phenomenon, The Great British Bake Off, this musical serves up a deliciously funny and heart-warming celebration of baking, friendship, and competition! Follow 8 amateur bakers as they whisk, knead, and sing their way through the nation's favourite baking competition, all under the watchful eyes of the judges and hosts. Packed with catchy songs, laugh-out-loud moments, and plenty of theatrical treats, this feel-good musical is perfect for the whole family. Expect cakes, chaos, and showstopping performances in a production guaranteed to leave audiences smiling.

Manannan's Winterfest № 9
events.description: Manannan’s Winterfest returns to the Gaiety Theatre in a unique concert celebrating Manx Christmas traditions through a collaboration of the Island’s finest exponents of classical, folk, brass and choral music, with a sprinkle of local humour and drama added to the mix! The mighty Sea-God Manannan invites you to get into the Manx festive spirit and join him for this very special evening of entertainment!

events.title: SPARK - Reach for the Stars
events.description: Rocket into space with Nat as she overcomes her fears and strives to achieve her greatest ambition – to fly. Told through dazzling puppetry and inspired by the life of Mae Jemison, the first African American woman to go into space, this heart-warming and inspiring story encourages us all to strive for our goals. Created by Little Angel Theatre , a children’s puppetry theatre in North London renowned for using the magic and wonder of puppetry to fuel young imaginations, this inspiring production is suitable for children aged 5 - 11. 🌟 Reach for the Stars forms part of SPARK Family Festival, returning for its third year on Sunday 4th October. This year, SPARK is taking families on an out-of-this-world adventure with a Space theme.

events.title: Active Souls Astronaut Training School
events.description: Active Souls are inviting young space explorers to get active, have fun and prepare for their mission beyond the stars! From astronaut-inspired challenges to fun physical activities, budding astronauts will put their strength, agility, coordination and teamwork to the test as they take on their very own astronaut training missions. And this time, Active Souls are bringing their out-of-this-world adventure to the Royal Hall, transforming it into an astronaut training school.

The Very Hungry Caterpillar Show
events.description: The Very Hungry Caterpillar Show has been dazzling audiences around the globe for over ten years, faithfully bringing Eric Carle’s timeless classics to the stage. Created by Jonathan Rockefeller, the critically acclaimed show features a menagerie of over 75 magical and larger-than-life puppets, including the star of the show –The Very Hungry Caterpillar. Alongside The Very Hungry Caterpillar, the show features three other Eric Carle stories. These beloved tales are brought to life by a captivating cast of storytellers, sweeping original music, and stunning puppetry. Celebrating 10 years on stage, the multi-award-winning and nominated show, has performed in over 20 countries to more than 3 million children, receiving universal acclaim from The New York Times, The Chicago Tribune, Time Out, The Huffington Post and more. We invite you and your loved ones on an unforgettable journey that will delight anyone from ages 1 to 99, as The Very Hungry Caterpillar jumps off the page and onto the stage! It’s truly one VERY magical hour. REVIEW QUOTES “Beautiful, Rhythmic, and Faithful to the Author’s Works. A Triumph!” - Time Out “We Rate It Five Smiles.” - Newsday “Colorful, Engaging, Charming.” - The Huffington Post “Bedazzling! Will Mesmerize Audiences!” - The New York Times “Your Favorite Small Person Will Be Changed for the Better.” - Live Theatre UK “Refreshing, Clever, and a Great Time. Brings the Work of Eric Carle to Life!” - NY Theatre Guide “A Knock Out Success!” Daily Telegraph

events.title: Jimmy Carr: Killing Jokes (On Sale Friday 23rd October)
events.description: In comedy, 'killing' is a good thing. Everywhere else, it's frowned upon. Jimmy has confirmed kills in over 50 countries and on 13 specials. Eyewitnesses describe it as 'a brutal, hilarious, life affirming night out’. The brand-new show is packed with fast, dark one-liners about all kinds of terrible things. But they are just jokes. They're not the terrible things. Jokes are like magnets. They attract some people and repel others. You can joke about anything, but not with anyone. If you’re attracted to Jimmy's brand of comedy and think you can take the jokes, then by all means come out and play. If you think you'd be offended, then stay away. At this point, being offended at a Jimmy Carr show is like buying a ticket to a horror movie and complaining you got scared. Don’t be a dummy. Look, if you’ve read this far, we know you want to come. So hurry up and buy a ticket. It’ll sell out, so don’t miss out.

events.title: Saturday Night Fever
events.description: Disco is back on the Rock! Get ready to dust off your flares and hit the dance floor as the acclaimed Douglas Choral Union—the powerhouse creative team behind the sensational Chicago—brings the ultimate 1970s phenomenon, Saturday Night Fever, straight to the stage of the Gaiety Theatre. Set against the gritty backdrop of Brooklyn, this electrifying musical follows Tony Manero, a young paint store clerk who finds escape and glory as the undisputed king of the local discotheque. When he teams up with the talented Stephanie Mangano for a high-stakes dance competition, his world changes forever. Featuring spectacular choreography, era-defining swagger, and the legendary soundtrack written by the Isle of Man’s very own Manx-born icons, the Bee Gees, this high-energy production is packed with timeless anthems including "Stayin' Alive," "Night Fever," "Tragedy," and "How Deep Is Your Love.” Don't miss a night of big dances, bigger hair, and non-stop nostalgia. Prove that disco is alive and well on the Isle of Man! Be sure not to miss out on the Odyssey Stage Experience!

events.title: Phantom of the Opera
events.description: Experience the magic, mystery, and romance of Phantom of the Opera, one of the world’s most beloved musical theatre productions. Taylorian Productions proudly presents our version of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s incredible musical at the Gaiety Theatre from 1st-14th August 2027. Set beneath the grandeur of the Paris Opera House, this captivating story follows the talented young soprano Christina Daaé (Alexandra Slater) whose extraordinary voice captures the attention of a mysterious masked figure known as the Phantom (Damian Kneale). Living in the shadows beneath the opera house, he becomes Christine’s secret mentor, but his growing obsession leads to a thrilling tale of love, jealousy, and intrigue. Featuring unforgettable music, dramatic storytelling, and a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere, Phantom of the Opera promises a mesmerising experience filled with emotion, suspense, and spectacle. Suitable for the entire family, this is a wonderful opportunity to experience the magic of live theatre and discover a timeless story that has enchanted audiences around the world. We can’t wait to welcome you to the Gaiety Theatre in August.

events.title: A Level Up Club Event: Theatre Trip to Legally Blonde
events.description: A Level Up Club Event: Theatre Trip to Legally Blonde 💗 DM US ON SOCIALS TO BOOK 💗 Pink power + big ambition Join us for Legally Blonde at the Gaiety. Girls’ night, main character energy, zero mark-ups. Okay but… what’s more Level Up than pink power, big ambition, and proving everyone wrong? On Tuesday 12 May at 7.30pm, we’re heading to see Legally Blonde The Musical at the beautiful Gaiety Theatre and honestly… it feels VERY us. Elle Woods starts with heartbreak and ends up at Harvard Law. Along the way she finds her confidence, her voice, and her people. It’s fun, it’s fierce, it’s funny, and basically a reminder that you can be smart, stylish, kind and ambitious all at once. And we’re turning it into a proper girls’ night out✨ 🎟️ The Details £27.30 per ticket (including booking fees for Villa Gaiety) We’ll buy the tickets as a group No added fees, no mark-ups for Level Up - this is just a fun outing together Just DM us to secure yours, and we'll send you link for payment. Easy. Stress-free. Sorted. 💗 The Plan We’ll meet before the show at Frank Matcham's for drinks if you fancy making a full evening of it. Then we’ll head in together, ready to cheer, laugh and maybe shed a tiny emotional tear during “So Much Better”. Think theatre trip meets confidence boost meets wholesome midweek reset. Because sometimes growth looks like workshops and big conversations. Sometimes it looks like belting show tunes with your girls and heading home feeling unstoppable. events.title: Citywide Garage Sale (City of Ramsey & City of Elk River)
events.description: Citywide Garage Sale (City of Ramsey & City of Elk River) The City of Elk River and the City of Ramsey are teaming up once again for the 2026 Citywide Garage Sale.About this EventMeet your neighbors, discover great bargains, and hunt for hidden treasures at the fourth annual City-wide Garage Sale, happening May Thursday, May 14 through Saturday, May 16! We are excited to team up with Elk River again to co-host our Garage Sales on the same weekend in order to expand the shopping experience.In order to have your sale included in the Citywide Garage Sale master list, this form must be submitted by Monday, May 11 at 12:00 p.m. The complete list will be available on the city's website on Tuesday, May 12 at 10:00 a.m. The map and sales list will be final. No cancellations will be updated.Learn more or register (Elk River): https://bit.ly/3TmX1n3Learn more or register (Ramsey): https://www.ci.ramsey.mn.us/941/Garage-Sale-TrailOn Sunday, May 17, we encourage sellers to host a "free day" and/or donate leftover items. A list of local .Garage Sale Safety TipsIf you are planning a garage sale at your house, here are some tips to remember.Always have at least two people working.Lock the doors into your home and do not let shoppers into your house to try on clothes or use the bathroom—post a sign stating a bathroom/changing area is not available.Keep only a minimal amount of cash on site.Keep the money on you at all times, not on a table. A fanny pack or money belt usually works well.Have a phone close by to report any suspicious activity.Do not accept checks.Place expensive items near you.Try to place all items outside of the garage and keep the garage door shut.Be observant and wary of distractions.Acknowledge all shoppers.Do not advertise the sale as a “Moving Sale,” which implies the house may be vacant for extended periods.Do not answer questions about alarm systems and daytime/nighttime occupancy.Do not buy or sell used car seats.City Ordinance restricts the number of sales at a residence to two per year, each lasting no longer than five days. Always obtain permission from the owner before posting signs on another’s property. For more information on having a garage sale and other home safety tips, contact the Ramsey Police Department at 763-427-6812. events.title: Sulby River Kayak Trip
events.description: Sulby River Kayak Trip 🛶 Escape onto the beautiful, wild and sheltered Sulby River to connect to the elements and have an adventure. 🌳 We jump into our very stable glass bottom sit on top kayaks, relax and travel into this sheltered nature reserve. 🕊 We often see the beautiful Little Egret, Herons, Barnacle and Cananda geese and sometimes the elusive kingfisher. 😌 Come and join us for a relaxing float as we then make our way down through the reeds and the trees as we explore this hidden stretch of river. 🌿 We will stop to try some foraged food including - tri-corned leek, wild spinach. The Sulby river is the longest river on the Island and offers slow-moving and flat water for an easy paddle for beginners in double or single kayaks. We have warm waterproof salopette trousers to keep your legs and core feeling toasty warm if you need them. We never expect to get wet and we launch with our feet dry. To book please visit: https://happyexplorer.co.uk/event/sulby-river-kayak-trip/ We will meet outside Ramsey Swimming Pool. events.title: FREE evening 6 week Manx taster course - 'Blass: a taste of Manx' (ST. JOHN'S)
events.description: FREE evening 6 week Manx taster course - 'Blass: a taste of Manx' (ST. JOHN'S) Are you curious about the Manx language and keen to learn more? Then there’s a course for you! Culture Vannin is delighted to invite adult beginners to join in with a FREE six-week introductory course: Blass: A Taste of Manx. This friendly, fun, and welcoming course will offer participants the opportunity to learn useful, everyday phrases, explore the fascinating history of Manx, and discover the language that is all around us through place names and common words. Whether you’ve been here all your life, or are new to the Island, Blass (Manx for ‘taste’) will help you to begin your journey into the Manx language. The courses will start week beginning 23rd February for in-person sessions, with the online course starting at the beginning of March. There are three time slots to choose from (just sign up to one!) * Tuesday lunchtimes – 1.10pm–1.50pm at Douglas City Hall * Wednesday evenings – 7pm–8pm at Culture Vannin, St John’s * Thursday evenings – 7pm–8pm online via Zoom This listing is for the weekly sessions taking place on Wednesday evenings between Wednesday 25th February – Wednesday 1st April in ST JOHN'S, but you can sign up to any of the sessions via SurveyMonkey: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/R9TWK9P No prior knowledge is required, or expected, and adult participants aged 16+ will be very welcome to take part. These 6-week courses are taking place as part of Blein ny Gaelgey, Year of the Manx Language; a year-long celebration of Manx, which aims to encourage more people to hear, see and use the language in their everyday lives. Throughout the year, special events, activities and learning opportunities are taking place to highlight that Manx is a living community language which belongs to everyone. Find out more about the year at www.yearofmanx.im Also check out other Workshops in Peel.

events.title: Luck Lore and Legends
events.source: manx radio & manx national heritage & allevents (ramsey)
events.description: Luck Lore and Legends 🍀 Luck, Lore & Legends at The Grove ✨ Discover what brought good luck to a Victorian Manx home and what might invite misfortune through the door? Step inside The Grove for a fascinating guided tour exploring the traditions, folklore and superstitions that once shaped everyday life on the Isle of Man. Discover the curious beliefs surrounding luck, love, weddings, death, weather and the fairies, and find out why generations followed particular customs, carried lucky charms and observed household rituals. 🍀 Discover charms and customs believed to bring good fortune 💍 Uncover superstitions surrounding love and marriage 🌦️ Explore traditional beliefs about weather and the seasons 🧚 Hear tales of fairies and Manx folklore 🏠 Find out how superstition influenced everyday Victorian life From the familiar to the wonderfully strange, uncover the beliefs and traditions that still linger behind the walls of this historic Manx home. ✨ Join us at The Grove and discover a world of luck, lore and legend. Suitable for adults and older children (recommended age 12+). Tickets: £10 per person plus an optional donation to our Charity Also check out other Nonprofit events in ramsey.

events.title: CEO. Angel. Founder. The lessons Chris Hall learned along the way
events.description: CEO. Angel. Founder. The lessons Chris Hall learned along the way CEO of the island's phone company. Then an angel investor. Then a founder raising his own money. Chris Hall on what each stage taught him.About this EventThe Isle of Man's phone company launched Europe's first live 3G network. It missed the world first to Japan's Docomo by a matter of weeks. The local headline read "Sushi 1, Kippers nil."The man running it was Chris Hall. At 50 he walked away from the CEO job and started backing other people's startups as an angel. Then he co-founded one himself, and had to go and ask for the money.That startup is Stacuity. It started with Isle of Man angel money and closed a multi-million-pound Series A in 2025.So he's sat on both sides of the table. Tonight we ask him what that looks like from each chair.What we'll get into:Running a corporate from the inside, and knowing when to leaveLife after the CEO job: boards, portfolios and "being a pluralist"What an angel checks before writing a cheque, and what makes him say noWhy he picked Stacuity, and why he joined rather than just investedPitching as a founder after years of being pitched toRaising from island angels, then from a VCWhat you can build from here that you can't build from LondonWho it's for:Founders getting ready to raise. Corporate folk wondering if they've got a startup or an angel cheque in them. Anyone who's ever pitched and wondered what the person across the table was thinking.Free to attend.Where: Launchpad Event Space, Hillary House, Prospect Hill, Douglas, IM1 1EQWhen: Thursday 29 October 2026, 17:30Hosted by Launchpad, the Isle of Man's Builder's Playground. Also check out other in Douglas.

events.description: Little Spooky Cinema – Coco We are bringing Disney Pixar’s modern masterpiece back to the big screen, offering an unforgettable cinematic escape that celebrates the power of family, memory, and chasing your dreams. The adventure follows Miguel, a young boy with a secret passion for music, which is strictly forbidden by his family of generations of shoemakers. On the Day of the Dead, a mysterious chain of events accidentally transports him to the colourful Land of the Dead. To find his way home, Miguel teams up with a charming trickster named Héctor. Together, they embark on an extraordinary journey to unlock the real story behind Miguel’s family history, creating a beautiful mix of laugh-out-loud comedy, vibrant culture, and genuinely breathtaking musical moments. Perfect for all generations, this crowd-pleasing screening provides a warm, relaxed atmosphere for the whole family. Parents get a deeply moving story about honouring our roots, kids get a spectacle of colour and giggles, and everyone leaves with a song in their heart. events.title: Hop tu Naa Festival 2026 at Cregneash
events.description: Hop tu Naa Festival 2026 at Cregneash Cregneash hosts its annual Manx Hop tu Naa Festival, a key highlight of the October half term programme. Hop tu Naa is a New Year festival rooted in the Celtic calendar. It shares links with wider Gaelic traditions, including Scotland’s Hogmanay. The festival marks the end of the harvest and the shift into longer nights, traditionally a time of reflection, thanks, and community celebration. The event brings Manx customs to life through hands-on activity, music, storytelling, and food traditions across the historic village. Visitors can take part in: Carving their own spooky moot (turnip) lantern Live Manx music and a community sing-along of the Hop tu Naa song with Matt Kelly Traditional dances including Peree Bane and Skeddan Jiarg Herbal charm making in Jinny the Witch’s Cottage Arts and crafts in the Harvest Craft Cottage Hollantide Gingerbread making in the Kitchen of Church farm Manx fairytale storytelling by the fire in Church Farm Parlour Salt dough Hollantide Fairings in Quirks Croft The festival combines living history, music, and family-friendly activities to bring Manx seasonal traditions into a hands-on, accessible setting. Useful information Suitable for families and children of all primary school ages Includes craft, storytelling, music, food demos, and outdoor activities Turnip carving (moot lanterns) Some activities take place outdoors, so please dress for the weather We recommend sturdy footwear due to uneven ground in the village Everyone attending needs a ticket Some activities operate on a timed or capacity basis and may involve short waits at peak times

events.description: Extraordinary Fungi - Wildlife Watch (4-12 years old) Embark on a fungi adventure! Wander, learn, and marvel at the colours on the forest floor! Fungi come in all shape, colours and forms and surprise us at every turn. When we observe them in more detail, they keep on surprising us even more! events.title: Wild and Waiting Things - ALBUM LAUNCH
events.description: Wild and Waiting Things - ALBUM LAUNCH Join this year’s Biosphere Artist in Residence, Alice Dudley, for an evening of live music, special guests, and a pop-up art exhibition to celebrate the launch of her album ‘Wild and Waiting Things’. 📆 Saturday 7th November 📍 Erin Arts Centre ⏰ Doors 7:00pm, 7:30 Start 🎟️ Tickets £10 The culmination of a year-long residency, ‘Wild and Waiting’ things is an album inspired by traditional Manx folk tales and based around the concept of an enchanted forest, featuring the voices of some familiar figures from Manx folklore. With each song inspired by a specific tale and set in an enchanted version of our landscape, Alice’s reimagining of classic Manx tales seeks to align the magic of folklore with the real-life magic of the natural world. As both a visual artist and a songwriter, Alice’s practice has been shaped by our Island and its stories. Her main goal this year was to encourage collaboration and connection with our Island and with each other, encouraging creatives to work together to make something that celebrated our landscape, our language, our stories, and the shared sense of belonging they can offer us. Bringing together the arts, nature, and community has been at the very heart of her residency, from her own body of work to the outdoor workshops, live music events, and collaborative projects she has organised this year. The evening will feature special guests performances from Matt Kelly and Mike and Ian (The Ballaghs) and an exclusive live debut of Alice’s album ‘Wild and Waiting Things’ in its entirety. A further aspect of the evening will be a pop-up exhibition showcasing the results of some of the collaborative artwork made at various Manx Wildlife Trust events throughout the summer, including an opportunity to view the postcards created as part of ‘O Vannin Veg Veen’, a community postcard project. Meaning ‘Dear Little Island’ in Manx, the project has been designed and curated by Alice and features creative responses from artists and writers of all ages, including a series of collaborative postcards which bring together two creative voices on the same piece. The Biosphere Artist in Residence scheme is hosted by the Manx Wildlife Trust, and supported by the Isle of Man Arts Council in partnership with UNESCO Biosphere Isle of Man and Culture Vannin. events.title: What actually is PR? Why it matters and how to make it work for you
events.description: What actually is PR? Why it matters and how to make it work for you What actually is PR? Why it matters and how to make it work for your organisationAbout this EventMost businesses know they should be "doing PR" but not so many understand what PR really is, how it differs from marketing, and how to use PR to effectively support business goals.In this interactive two-hour workshop, led by Isle of Man-based PR consultant Kirstie Nickson Chart.PR, you'll learn exactly what strategic PR looks like and how it can help build reputation, increase trust, attract new opportunities and support your business's growth.Through practical exercises, real-life examples and group discussion, you'll learn:What PR actually is (and isn't)The difference between PR, marketing and advertisingHow to align your PR activity with your business goalsHow to identify and secure PR opportunities for your organsiationWhether you're a business owner, marketing professional, charity leader or a start-up founder, you'll leave with a clearer understanding of the importance of PR, its role in your organisation's success and practical ideas you can put into action straight away.Who's it for?This workshop is suitable for:Business founders who want to understand more about PR, its role in the business and gain practical tips for their organisation;In-house marketing teams who want to upskill in the area of strategic PR;Charities and smaller organisations who want to be more visible but don't have the resource/budget to outsource to a PR agencyAbout the hostThis workshop is hosted by Kirstie Nickson Chart.PR, Co-Founder and Director of Sidekick, a PR consultancy that helps organisations build trust, protect reputation and achieve measurable business outcomes through strategic public relations.Manx-born and bred, Kirstie returned to the Isle of Man in 2022 after building a career spanning almost 20 years at PR agencies in Sheffield, working with organisations across the UK and Europe, from ambitious SMEs to international brands operating in sectors including hospitality, healthcare, professional services, leisure, education and the third sector.As the Isle of Man's first and only CIPR Chartered PR Practitioner to date, Kirstie brings a unique combination of internationally recognised professional standards and real-world agency experience.Founded in 2016 by Kirstie, Charlotte Dimond FCIPR Chart.PR and Eve Worthington, Sidekick PR is known for combining strategic thinking with practical delivery, helping clients achieve their business goals through reputational management and effective communication.Now based in Ramsey, Kirstie is excited to bring Sidekick PR's expertise to the local business community through the agency's first public workshop on the Island, helping organisations better understand how PR can support growth, reputation and long-term success. events.title: An Evening with Sir Alastair Cook CBE.
events.description: An Evening with Sir Alastair Cook CBE. Hosted by the brilliant Geoff Miller OBE, former England cricketer & selector, who is a highly respected figure on the after dinner circuit!About this EventSir Alastair Nathan Cook CBE is England's leading Test Run scorer of all time and is coming to the Isle of Man as our guest speaker, on Thursday 12th November 2026, at an event sponsored by Standard Bank (Isle of Man).The 41-year-old Gloucester born cricket legend played in 161 test matches and scored 12,472 runs.Universally acknowledged as an opening batsman of immense poise, grit and skill, Sir Alastair made his debut with the Test side in 2006 and became England’s all-time leading run scorer in 2015. He captained the Team from 2012 to 2016, is a three-time Ashes winner and the 5th highest run-scorer in the history of Test Cricket.Cook’s unique talent and flair, combined with outstanding leadership qualities, relentless drive and commitment, have propelled him to the Olympian Heights.There is an interesting musical link to his career success. As a chorister and boarding pupil at St Paul’s Cathedral School, a hectic practice and rehearsal schedule imbibed the young Alastair with what was to become his legendary resilience and self-discipline.The evening will be hosted by the brilliant Geoff Miller OBE, former England cricketer and selector, who is a highly respected figure on the after dinner speaking circuit. Geoff is sure to have our audience in raptures, with a plethora of amusing recollections and in depth analysis of the game he loves. These qualities have seen him twice voted Sporting Speaker of the Year and Cricket Speaker of the Year for the past 4 years.Tickets:Members: £65.00 p/p exc VAT. events.description: Sea Thief by Jackie Morrey-Grace Friday 13 November 7.30pm Tickets: £15 A double-bill premiere of original folk-poetry theatre and the official book launch of Sea Thief & Other Horrors by multi-award-winning writer and performer Jackie Morrey-Grace. Jackie's first live production in over two years opens with a new folk-theatre adaptation of the title poem from her fourth Isle of Man Arts Council-funded poetry collection, Sea Thief & Other Horrors. Inspired by Jackie's love of Dvořák's symphonic poems, particularly The Noon Witch, this dark folk tale blends poetry, music and song. Alongside Jackie, it will feature Blue Vannin Jazz Club’s Musical Director John Stillman on violin, Jackie's husband Ed Morrey on percussion, and opening scenes performed by jazz vocalist Lauren Gray, and sound artist Amy Howse. Part Two presents a full mask, music and movement production of Jackie's second poetry publication, Asila's Song. This haunting tale of curlews and bones lost at sea again features John Stillman, this time on the Erin Arts Centre Steinway, musicians, Lauren Gray, Amy Howse and Ed Morrey, plus dancers Owen Atkinson and Ash Gibson, with the epic poem being performed by Jackie herself. Jackie's self-illustrated books, including Sea Thief & Other Horrors, will be available to purchase during the interval and after the performance for £10 each. This show is written, performed and produced by Jackie Morrey-Grace and Penny Productions. events.description: Rushen Players present Good Things Rushen Players present Good Things by Liz Lochhead Tickets: Adults £12, Over 65s £10, Under 18s £5 Good Things by Liz Lochead, first performed in 2004, is a romantic farce set in a charity shop. Suddenly single and with the dreaded Big Five-0 staring her in the face, Susan Love – a charity shop volunteer – also has to cope with a father in his second childhood, a daughter in the throes of aggravated adolescence and an ex who, unfortunately, still has the power to wound. Set in the charity shop on three different days in one year – 6th January, Valentine’s Day and Christmas Eve – Good Things is a poignant, hilarious and sympathetic play with a lot to say about finding love later in life while still retaining humour, sanity and dignity. events.description: Digital Isle 2026 Join us for the sixth annual Digital Isle – the premier event for the Isle of Man’s rapidly growing tech ecosystem!About this EventTaking place on Thursday 26 November at the Comis Hotel, Digital Isle 2026 brings together the Island’s digital, technology and business community alongside leading voices from further afield for a day of valuable industry insight, collaboration and conversations around what’s changing – and what it means for the Isle of Man.Across the 2026 agenda, we'll explore how the Island can stay agile, adapt and make the most of the opportunities ahead. Key topics will include what it means to treat data as an asset, how AI is changing the way we work, what businesses need from the workforce of the future, and how digital transformation is reshaping government and healthcare.We’ll also look beyond the technology itself to the wider forces influencing the Island’s digital economy, including what investors are looking for, regulation as a competitive advantage and global digital access – bringing perspectives from those working at the heart of these areas.The full Digital Isle 2026 agenda is currently being finalised and will be published in the coming weeks, with further speakers and session details to be announced very soon.Why be there?For returning attendees and those joining us for the first time, Digital Isle 2026 is a chance to understand what’s changing, where new opportunities are emerging and what those developments could mean for you and your organisation.Alongside key announcements across sessions and panels, the event creates space for open discussion and the conversations that follow. It’s a chance to reconnect with familiar faces, meet people you might not otherwise cross paths with and come away with new ideas, perspectives and insights.What to expectA look at what’s taking shape: hear the latest from Digital Isle of Man and explore the priorities, opportunities and developments set to influence the future of the Island’s digital landscape.Ideas worth talking about: join expert panels and thought-provoking discussions on the opportunities and challenges transforming the Island’s digital landscape.Engaging networking: meet people from across the Island and beyond, make new connections and create space for valuable conversations and introductions.Perspectives from across the sector: hear from local and international voices bringing different experiences and expertise to the conversation.Innovation Challenge 2027 first look: we’ll be unveiling the next Innovation Challenge theme, with a first look at what’s ahead.A chance to be part of what comes next: Digital Isle 2026 isn't only about reflecting on where we are today. It’s an opportunity to see where things are heading and connect with the people helping move them forward.Each year, Digital Isle brings you closer to the people, ideas and conversations influencing what comes next for the Island’s digital future – all completely free to attend.Interested in sponsorship?Digital Isle provides opportunities for businesses and organisations to support the annual event and engage with the Island’s digital community through sponsorship. events.title: LOOKS Campaign Premiere - Free Online Event
events.description: An online event, open to everyone on the Isle of Man and beyond. On Tuesday 1 December 2026, from 5:00 to 7:00 PM (18:00-20:00 CET), a free meeting in English opens the LOOKS campaign. You can join from home - there is no fee and no registration. LOOKS is an educational and cultural project about appearance and aesthetics, and its foundation is oral health. It asks how the face develops over a lifetime and why the smile carries so much weight in the way people see one another. Documentary film, animation and fine art are the tools it uses to tell that story. The meeting presents the project, its educational aims and the materials it shares openly. The campaign includes a feature documentary and an online series, alongside a free educational section written for non-specialists. LOOKS is created by Pawel Lipka, a painter and animator who has worked on The Garfield Show and on visual effects for the feature film Suicide Room. More information: https://looksphilosophy.com/education

events.description: The Makers Social Club: Christmas Patchwork Evening Join MNH Crafters for a cosy festive evening of traditional Manx craft, Christmas treats and a little time to get creative. Taking inspiration from the Manx National Heritage collections, you’ll learn how to make your own traditional Manx Log Cabin patchwork square. This style of patchwork has been made on the Isle of Man since the early 19th century and was traditionally used to create blankets, bedspreads and cushions, bringing warmth and colour into Manx homes. Settle in at 1 Market Square and enjoy festive snacks and non-alcoholic Christmas drinks while you learn the techniques and create your own patchwork square to take home. All materials are provided, so just bring yourself and get ready for a relaxed evening of Manx craft and Christmas creativity. Useful information Suitable for adults and older teens. No previous sewing or patchwork experience is required. All materials are provided. Your ticket includes festive snacks and non-alcoholic festive drinks. The workshop takes place at 1 Market Square. Please arrive a few minutes early so you can get settled before the workshop begins. You’ll make one traditional Manx patchwork square to take home.

events.description: The Manx Breast Cancer Support Group are really pleased to be bringing ‘Rule The World’ to the Isle of Man. Recognised as the Number 1 Take That tribute act in the world, they recently appeared alongside Nicole Kidman, Hugh Bonneville, Julie Walters and THE REAL TAKE THAT on BBC1’s ‘The Graham Norton Show’. events.title: back_to_the_outback_2.exe: The Xmas Y2K to 2010s Reunion
events.venue: The Outback, Barrack Street, Im1 2Af Douglas, Isle Of Man, Isle Of Man
events.description: back_to_the_outback_2.exe: The Xmas Y2K to 2010s Reunion Before the group chat, there was a text (or an MSN nudge) saying “Outback?” and an outfit you genuinely thought you looked the business in. Top Shop or Miss Selfridges in The Strand, then you’d spend ages getting ready, and the evidence was either a blurry photo of six people and someone’s thumb or a 200-photo Facebook album. If you were coming from up north, that meant the number 3 into town. Your mates got on at the Manxie, the top deck was the pre-drinks, and the whole lot of you were clomping down the stairs before it had even stopped. “Please sit down till the bus stops, THANK YOU.” We did it last year. You lot bought the DJ (me, Ryan) so many pints I headbutted the balcony railing packing my stuff away. By the end of the night there were LED foam batons all over Snapchat and half the kebab shops in Douglas. So we're doing it again, this time with the 2000s and 2010s. Timbaland to Clubland, R&B one minute and pure cheese the next, with the OB favourites in there too. Teenage Dirtbag and Land Down Under will get their outing. We know where we are. Dress up if you fancy it. This was the decade Kelly Rowland tried to text Nelly on Excel, so the bar’s not high. If the Henleys hoodie or the going-out top is still knocking about at the back of the wardrobe, this is its night out. Put your phone in your pocket and have a dance. It’s the Isle of Man, someone will tell you what you got up to anyway. Get onto the ones you used to go with, especially the one who’s been saying “we need a night out” since the last one. You’ve got till Christmas to recover. back_to_the_outback_2.exe: The Xmas Y2K to 2010s Reunion Saturday 19 December 2026 · The Outback, Douglas 4pm–9pm · Last entry 8pm Also check out other Trips & Adventurous Activities in Douglas.

events.description: Hospice Isle of Man is an official international charity of Tokyo Marathon 2027!We have just two exclusive places available to take on the iconic Tokyo Marathon and raise money for Hospice!Run one of the Abbott World Marathon Majors on a flat, fast course through Tokyo’s buzzing streets, past ancient temples, the soaring Skytree and the neon glow of Ginza.The 2027 race marks its 20th anniversary, the perfect year to be part of something unforgettable while supporting an incredible cause.These places are highly sought after, and we want to hear from you if you would like to compete and raise money at the same time. The race has a suggested minimum fundraising donation for Hospice of £4,000, but there is nothing to pay upfront.Applicants will be notified on the 28th May if successful. events.title: Welfare Officer Training: Time to Listen
events.venue: Isle Of Man Sport High Performance Centre
events.description: Welfare Officer Training: Time to Listen Understand the Welfare Officer role, develop key skills, and learn how to effectively support and safeguard childrenAbout this EventLearn about the responsibilities connected with being a Welfare Officer, the skills needed to excel in the role, and how you can ensure that you’re supporting and safeguarding children effectively.Developed in partnership with NSPCC and CPSUOverviewLearn about the responsibilities connected with being a Welfare Officer, the skills needed to excel in the role, and how you can ensure that you’re supporting and safeguarding children effectively Every child deserves to enjoy playing sport and engaging in physical activity in a safe and supportive environment, where they feel heard, understood, and valued. On this online classroom, learn how you can support, empower, and safeguard children participating in sport and physical activity in your capacity as a welfare officer.This interactive face-to-face workshop will give you an essential understanding of what is required of welfare officers that are responsible for managing and reporting concerns about children, and for putting into place procedures to safeguard children, ensuring that you have the practical knowledge required to take a child-focused approach and excel in the role.You will also learn about the importance of building relationships and trust with the key people that you’ll be working with, essential to working with colleagues to safeguard children effectively.Through interactive scenarios featuring people from different sports and activities, you will also practise your decision-making in a safe and supportive environment, enabling you to explore some possible consequences of your decisions. This will help to prepare you to act in similar scenarios as a welfare officer, giving you crucial confidence in your ability to act in each child’s best interest.Book your place on the workshop today to develop your skills and support your growth as a great child-focused welfare officer.The course has been awarded 1.5 CPD points by the Chartered Institute for the Management of Sport and Physical Activity (CIMSPA).On this course you will learn:How a welfare officer works with others to create a child-centred environmentHow the role of the welfare officer fits into the wider safeguarding environmentHow safeguarding fits into the wider culture of your organisationHow to respond to and report concernsHow you can support your coaches to protect themselves.This workshop is being organised by Manx Sport and Recreation and will take place in the Isle of Man Sport High Performance Centre meeting room.Venue Directions - Isle of Man Sport High Performance CentreTravelling south on the A5 Castletown New Road from Quarterbridge roundabout, after 50 yards take a left hand turn into the NSC outdoor venue. Turn left onto the roadways one way system and continue to car park one. The Isle of Man Sport High Performance Centre is located next to the athletics track.On entering the building take the stairs or lift to the first floor where you will find the meeting room.I f you need to cancel or make any changes to your booking, please contact us on aW9tc3BvcnQgfCBnb3YgISBpbQ== or call 688592 / 688557. events.description: Young Adult & Graduate Fair 2027 Ready to kick-start your career in the Isle of Man?About this EventLocate’s Young Adult and Graduate Fair is back for 2027!Whether you’re a recent graduate, looking for your first job, thinking about a career change, or wondering what your next move could be, come along and see what’s out there.📅 Wednesday 24 March 2027🕒 11am–4pm📍 Villa Marina, DouglasWhat can you expect?💼 Meet employersChat directly with businesses and organisations from across a wide range of sectors. Find out who’s hiring, what roles are available and what they’re looking for.🎤 Hear from people who’ve been thereOur Speaker Zone will return with talks and panel discussions featuring professionals from across the Island. Hear honest experiences, useful advice and different perspectives on building a career on Island.🏛️ NEW: Public Services Career ZoneThinking about a career in public services? Meet organisations from across the sector and find out about the different roles, career paths and opportunities available.🙌 NEW: Volunteer ZoneWant to gain experience, build your CV, learn new skills or simply give something back? events.title: Isle of Man Mini vs Ford - 2 icons. 1 legendary island.
events.description: Isle of Man Mini vs Ford - 2 icons. 1 legendary island. The Mini vs Ford Weekend brings together owners and enthusiasts of two of Britain’s most iconic car brands for a relaxed and enjoyable motoring tour on the Isle of Man. Created as a celebration of the friendly rivalry between Mini and Ford, the event is not a race or timed competition, but simply a fun way to enjoy great driving roads, great cars and great company. Throughout the weekend, participants take part in a programme of activities designed to make the most of the Island’s spectacular scenery. Scenic driving routes, group lunches and evening social events give everyone the chance to explore the Isle of Man while meeting fellow enthusiasts who share the same passion for these legendary marques. Visit iommotoringevents.com for more details. events.title: Dylan Moran
events.description: Showtime. What are you going to do? Are you going to go to work? Or stay in bed, chasing oblivion. Guess what? We're fresh out of oblivion. The Economy will do fine without you - but how long will you survive without the usual giant horn of frozen caramel latte and the five thousand other pieces of bullshit you have smushed together so you can point at it and croak ‘That’s my ..life?’ Now, now, all this drama and we’re not even out the door yet. Find out how it could all have been different. Find out how to reclaim your life by becoming a lethal kickboxing, chess champion. Pioneer new trends in global lovemaking, join tan elite band trillionaire poet/pastry chef/mountaineers. Just go LOOKING FOR TROUBLE A brand new show from BAFTA and Perrier awarding winning comedian & star of Black Books, Dylan Moran. “Joyfully cynical ” ★★★★★ - Metro “Perfect for the times” ★★★★★ - The i “Superb”★★★★ - Guardian “Trumping Shakespeare, he reduces life to four ages: “Child, failure, old and dead”.
